title: FEMA approves more than $3.9 million for North East Power fiber repairs
excerpt: Thaxton and Toccopola share a broadband link that NE SPARC crews worked on after the winter storm. The new federal award covers armored cable repairs.

paragraphs.text: FEMA approved more than $3.9 million to repair armored fiber-optic cables for the electric cooperative whose broadband network serves Thaxton and Toccopola. The Nov. 23 award names the cooperative as the recipient. The notice gives one amount for the project without breaking it down by county or identifying individual stretches of cable.

Residents in both communities share a connection through the Lafayette Springs substation. On Feb. 7, NE SPARC warned that splicing a cut cable on Highway 6 would interrupt internet service for subscribers connected there. The notice also named Delay, Hurricane and the east end of Toccopola Road. Crews planned to reconnect the line serving most customers first, then finish the section serving people west of Bethel Church Road.

The next morning, NE SPARC reported that all of its main transport lines were working again. Crews were still repairing the branches off those lines and the connections to individual customers. By spring 2022, the subsidiary of North East Mississippi Electric Power Association had extended internet access to parts of Pontotoc and Union counties beyond the cooperative’s electric service territory.

The award comes through FEMA’s Public Assistance program, which reimburses disaster recovery work through the state. The same announcement listed separate fiber repairs for the Alcorn County and Tishomingo County electric associations. Each of those awards is in addition to the North East Power amount.
